Floods Paralyze Key Sectors in Kazakhstan, Disrupting Trade and Transport

Severe flooding continues to sweep across central and northern Kazakhstan, bringing major economic disruption as authorities struggle to contain the disaster’s impact. Swollen rivers following days of heavy rainfall have inundated critical infrastructure, with the Ministry of Emergency Situations reporting that at least 8,000 homes and several industrial zones in Pavlodar, Karaganda, and Akmola regions remain underwater.

Transport links have been severely affected. Rail operator KazTransLines confirmed that freight traffic on major east-west corridors is halted, stranding shipments of grain and metals vital for export. “We are working around the clock, but the scale is unprecedented,” said spokesperson Aigul Sariyeva. Highways connecting Almaty to Astana have also been partially closed, causing supply chain delays and shortages of basic goods in some areas.

Agricultural unions warn of significant crop losses as fields remain submerged at the start of the spring planting season. “If the water does not recede within a week, we could lose up to 40% of our planned wheat output,” warned Yerlan Beketov, head of the National Farmers Council.

The National Bank of Kazakhstan stated it is closely monitoring the situation for inflationary risks, as food and fuel prices have already begun to climb in affected regions. Analysts at Steppe Financial Group expect the flooding to shave at least 1% off Kazakhstan’s GDP growth projection if disruptions persist through May.

With more rain forecast, officials are bracing for further evacuations and economic fallout. “Our priority is saving lives, but the economic recovery will be long and challenging,” said Deputy Prime Minister Nurzhan Tasmagambetov.
